title: Preservation for a general separated finite-type morphism
statement:
Fix the purity coefficient conventions [def-pur-conventions]:
$k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$,
a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and $n\geq1$, with
$A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Let $X,Y$ be finite-type
$k$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$ a separated finite-type $k$-morphism
[def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Use the
constructible exceptional inverse image $Rf^!$ of
[def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], whose adjunction relative to the
bounded constructible coefficient class is supplied by
[cor-sf-ambient-adjoint-discharge]; no unrestricted ambient exceptional
right adjoint datum is assumed. Then the analogues of the two preservation
clauses (2) and (3) of [def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility] hold
for this functor, with the following bounds.

If $X$ is nonempty, choose the finite affine charts
$U\subseteq f^{-1}(V)$ and closed presentations
$U\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^{d_U}_V$ of
[thm-pur-general-admissibility], with affine space understood as in
[def-sbc-affine-space], omitting empty charts. Put
$$
D=\max_U d_U,\qquad c_U=2(d_U+\dim Y),\qquad
c=\max_U\bigl(c_U+1+2(D-d_U)\bigr).
$$
Here dimension is Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension].
If $X$ is empty, put $D=c=0$ instead; there are no chart constants
$c_U$ to form (in particular no dimension of an empty $Y$ is needed).
For every pair of integers $a\leq b$:

1. $Rf^!$ carries $D_c^{[a,b]}(Y,A)$ into
$D_c^{[a-2D,b-2D+c]}(X,A)$, with constructible intervals as in
[def-weil-constructible-intervals].
2. If $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$, then
$Rf^!K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ has Tor amplitude in
$[a-2D,b-2D+c]$, in the sense of [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude].

proof.text:
The functor throughout is the constructible exceptional inverse
image, not an adjoint on all pro-etale complexes. The statement of
[cor-sf-ambient-adjoint-discharge] supplies precisely the adjunction
relative to the bounded constructible coefficient class at $A=A_{E,n}$
and explicitly excludes the unrestricted ambient datum. Thus no
all-sheaf pro-etale adjunction is used when applying the preservation
theorem below.

source.place: Statement: bounded constructible and finite-Tor scope of the two clauses

proof.text:
First handle $X=\varnothing$. In the small pro-etale site of
[def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], every object over $X$ is empty and is
covered by the empty family: for its empty affine open, the empty
finite family of affine opens has union equal to that open. The
sheaf axiom therefore forces its module of sections to
have one element. Every module sheaf and hence every complex on $X$ is
zero. The zero cohomology sheaves are constructible (use the empty
stratification, or the single empty stratum), and their support in
degrees is empty. The definitions [def-weil-constructible-intervals]
and [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] then put the zero output in every
required interval: its tensor product with any module sheaf is zero.
This proves both clauses with $D=c=0$, including $Y=\varnothing$.

source.place: Statement: maxima over the affine charts; empty-source completion

proof.text:
Now let $X$ be nonempty, so $Y$ is nonempty too. Use the
nonempty finite family of charts of [thm-pur-general-admissibility].
The chart clause in the statement of
[thm-pur-open-complement-unconditional] explicitly supplies the
open-complement condition for
$(W_U,\mathbf A^{d_U}_V)$ at $A=A_{E,n}$ with
$b_U=2(d_U+\dim V)$, and states the inequality
$d_U+\dim V\leq d_U+\dim Y$ for these charts. This is precisely the
chartwise open-complement bound prescribed by the source. Use this explicitly stated finite-stage specialization at
$A=A_{E,n}$ over $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$; no separate
coefficient-ring reduction is required.

source.place: Proof, chartwise open-complement bound; same-unit theorem at order 2080

proof.text:
For each chart $b_U\leq c_U=2(d_U+\dim Y)$. By
[def-exc-open-complement-bound], its condition with bound $b_U$
has two clauses. If $q>c_U$, then $q>b_U$, so the first clause gives
$R^qj_*M=0$ for every $A$-module sheaf $M$. Its second clause,
constructibility of $R^qj_*F$ for every constructible $F$ and every
integer $q$, does not involve the bound at all. These are precisely
the two clauses of the same condition with bound $c_U$. Thus every
chart satisfies the hypothesis with the constants in the statement.

source.place: Proof, hence also with the larger constant c_U; monotonicity written out

proof.text:
Apply [thm-pur-general-admissibility] to $f$ and these same
finite affine charts, with the constants $c_U$ established above.
Its hypotheses are the present separated finite-type morphism and the
chartwise open-complement conditions; its adjoints are used only on
the bounded constructible and finite-Tor coefficients as its statement
specifies. Its definitions of $D=\max_U d_U$ and
$c=\max_U(c_U+1+2(D-d_U))$ are identical to ours. Its first clause
therefore gives the asserted constructible cohomological interval
for every $a\leq b$, and its second gives the asserted Tor interval
and membership in $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$. This proves both conclusions
without assuming an ambient admissibility datum.

source.place: Proof, final sentence: its conclusion is the assertion

proof_origin.place: Proof paragraph, expanded using same-unit thm-pur-open-complement-unconditional and with scope and empty-source corrections

lean.note: Previously unstated prerequisite. States exactly the finite-coefficient chart assembly, using the published fixed-scalar module-sheaf coefficient presentation throughout, to avoid importing both legacy and reorganized UpperLowerStar declarations. The interval and Tor predicates are the existing upstream constructibleIn, constructibleFiniteTor and torAmplitudeIn, specialized to ModuleCat of the standard ULift of the actual quotient. At positive finite stages this constructibility is equivalent to the intrinsic notion by lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin. The real-data nonemptyCharts construction omits and finitely reindexes empty source charts internally while retaining both covers and every closed presentation. D and c use these surviving charts for nonempty X, and both are zero for empty X. The maximum formula for c is simplified algebraically to its common summand 2D+2dim(Y)+1. No open-complement or ambient-adjoint hypothesis is added. The owning module includes only a positive-stage specialization of the already recorded finiteTypeExceptionalInverseImage, installing its finite-coefficient and compactifiability witnesses from hn and c. The published exceptional dependency record is reused unchanged.

blueprint_update.statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter
([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting), let $f:X\to Y$ be a
separated finite-type
morphism. The ambient exceptional right adjoint datum of
[def-weil-ambient-exceptional-adjoint] is not assumed: on the bounded
constructible and finite-Tor coefficients of the two clauses below it is the
theorem [cor-sf-ambient-adjoint-discharge]. Then $f$
satisfies the two preservation clauses of
[def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility]: with the affine charts
$U\subseteq f^{-1}(V)$ and the integers $d_U$ of
[thm-pur-general-admissibility], put
$D=\max_Ud_U$ and $c_U=2\,(d_U+\dim Y)$. Then $Rf^!$ carries
$D_c^{[a,b]}(Y,A)$ into $D_c^{[a-2D,b-2D+c]}(X,A)$ for
$c=\max_U\bigl(c_U+1+2(D-d_U)\bigr)$, and it carries finite Tor
amplitude in $[a,b]$ to finite Tor amplitude in $[a-2D,b-2D+c]$.

proof.text:
For each chart the target $\mathbf A^{d_U}_V$ of the chartwise
presentation is of finite type over $k$ of dimension
$d_U+\dim V\leq d_U+\dim Y$. The open complement $W_U$ of $U$ in it
therefore satisfies the open-complement condition with constant
$2(d_U+\dim V)$ by [lem-exc-open-complement-known], hence also with
the larger constant $c_U=2(d_U+\dim Y)$, the condition being monotone
in its constant. The hypothesis of
[thm-pur-general-admissibility] is thus satisfied with these
constants, and its conclusion is the assertion.
